4646090.assessment: Three narrow, locally flat-baseline eclipses in sectors 4 and 31 give 10.7303766 d. Raw depths 1.95?2.26% and durations 2.75?3.46 h recur; the distinct custom extraction recovers all three at 0.59?0.64% aperture depth. Dilution differs between reductions. Source and independent gates pass; Gaia period and phase are feasible at the precision available.
4646090.source: Signed deficits in both sectors prefer the target. Free-Gaussian offsets are 0.46 and 2.28 arcsec, versus a capable TIC 4646088 neighbour 6.96 arcsec away (7.53 and 9.32 arcsec from fitted deficits). Fixed-neighbour / target SSE is 5.34 and 5.65 in sector stacks; per-event ratios 5.34,3.57,4.27 also favor target. These descriptive comparisons, repeated across sectors/events, support attribution; no calibrated PRF confidence is asserted.
4646090.geometry: Gaia orbit P=10.72678235 d. Representative photometric period 10.73037662 d; difference / Gaia quoted period error 1.05. Closest edge-on conjunction A: offset 0.612 d, covariance-linear error 0.457 d. Observed duration median 3.22 h; approximate central duration 8.06 h. These are feasibility diagnostics, not significance vetoes or a fitted geometry.
4646090.limitations: Gaia phase offset is 1.34 covariance-linear error units; grazing geometry can shorten the approximate central duration. No detailed physical fit or calibrated astrometric uncertainty.
4646090.next_check: Characterize dilution and grazing geometry if needed.

443106429.assessment: Four narrow raw eclipses in sectors 11 and 65 give 12.7955335 d, consistent with Gaia. Raw depths 1.82?2.84%, duration about 10.2 h; custom extraction recovers four at 1.84?3.33%. Eclipses are real and repeat, but the close host remains unresolved.
443106429.source: Sector 11 deficit lies 0.59 arcsec from target, with capable TIC 443106423 only 3.88 arcsec away; fixed-neighbour/target SSE 1.83 favors target. Extra fresh sector 65 was obtained; noisy one-event signed deficit has 13.4 arcsec fitted offset and close-neighbour/target SSE 0.99, failing independent separation. Source testing was attempted and remains scientifically ambiguous.
443106429.geometry: Gaia orbit P=12.79551859 d. Representative photometric period 12.79553346 d; difference / Gaia quoted period error 0.00. Closest edge-on conjunction A: offset -0.230 d, covariance-linear error 0.565 d. Observed duration median 10.23 h; approximate central duration 22.45 h. These are feasibility diagnostics, not significance vetoes or a fitted geometry.
443106429.limitations: Host not robustly separated from 3.88 arcsec capable neighbour; this is the one unresolved protocol gate.
443106429.next_check: Resolve target versusTIC 443106423 with higher spatial resolution eclipse photometry.

60443793.assessment: The original 6.510555 d search alias is wrong for the prominent eclipse train. Forty-eight raw minima give 1.29738064 d spacing; alternating depths imply a candidate 2.5947613 d binary period. Fresh imaging places these real EB photons off target, so the target-EB association is refuted. This is neither a confirmed target nor a target by-catch EB.
60443793.source: S 13/S 93 signed deficits are off target. Free-Gaussian offsets about 58 arcsec align with capable TIC 60443695 at 59.38 arcsec separation. Fixed-coordinate neighbour/target SSE 0.0032 and 0.0229 strongly favor that neighbour in two sectors; positive-clipped centroids alone give 44.7/50.2 arcsec. Scores are descriptive, with PRF/systematic caveats. Candidate neighbour identity is an inference, not a full adjudication of that star.
60443793.geometry: Gaia orbit P=6.51870479 d. Representative photometric period 2.59476129 d; difference / Gaia quoted period error -1927.55. Closest edge-on conjunction A: offset -1.217 d, covariance-linear error 0.569 d. Observed duration median 4.67 h; approximate central duration 243.51 h. These are feasibility diagnostics, not significance vetoes or a fitted geometry.
60443793.limitations: Neighbour EB period remains a candidate and has not undergone independent alias/geometry review as its own target. The target giant-radius estimate is also incompatible with interpreting this short period as its simple detached binary orbit.
60443793.gaia_association: photometric train does not trace target Gaia orbit

Trapezoid fits absorb smooth curvature and frequently hit duration/center bounds. The narrow-eclipse interpretation is refuted; binarity or ellipsoidal variability is not excluded.
428769301.source: Fresh first/last-sector cutouts were independently extracted. A meaningful narrow-event difference image cannot be defined from this smooth morphology; source gate was attempted and found no supported discrete eclipse to localize.
428769301.geometry: Gaia orbit P=3.73288066 d. No secure eclipse period exists for a meaningful conjunction/duration validation.
428769301.limitations: Physical variability mechanism remains unclassified. Smooth modulation alone does not establish eclipses.
428769301.next_check: No further eclipse follow-up required unless new discrete events appear.
